study.question: Which learned consumer accounts for the single-seed click-AUC loss when only the coarse-linear history moment is identified with its negative: the additive task adapter, the nonlinear context/history product branch, or their interaction?
study.hypothesis: Observed: the unchanged incumbent scores 0.6685268680, coarse-axis replacement 0.6667055158; adding a sign scalar to either pivot or target charts did not recover the gap (latest target-with-sign 0.6665929416 versus target-constant 0.6666401839, pivot-with-sign 0.6664435963 versus pivot-constant 0.6664137638). Scalar recoverability therefore has not demonstrated learnability. Provisional mechanism: signed coarse direction is mainly used by the context-conditioned product path. Exposing the original signed vector directly to that path alone will recover at least 75% of the contemporaneous both-signed minus both-axis AUC gap; exposing it only to the additive task adapter will recover at most 25%. Interpret these fractions only if the endpoint gap is positive and at least 0.0005. This is a conditional routing hypothesis, not proof that all sequence order is indispensable.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary mechanism lines227-283 read. Retain target-local activation, unnormalized pooling and the inherited task adaptation; test selective signed-moment availability to two existing consumers. Original LSTM null is dataset-specific, not local evidence. No originality claim.

Pinned forward175-200 flattens histories into a tokenizer. Retain incumbent compression and learned capacity rather than flattening or adding paired streams; vary only two consumers of one existing moment. Benchmark code is not an original-paper reproduction.

Pinned forward132-172 and block219-229 read: event and nonsequence tokens are retained in interaction layers. This proposal adds no tokens/attention/reduction; isolates sign availability in existing adapter and product routes. Original full paper unavailable in authorized bundle; priority unverified.
All existing learned modules, five moments and host training recipe inherited. Only the coarse moment supplied to each consumer changes, with endpoint bridge controls and no extra sign column.

inherited_components: Entire incumbent embedding/scorer/compression/support normalization/tower architecture and exact initialization sequence
All five target-match/local/coarse/quadratic/duplicate moments and original gates
Task-specific residual adapters and blockwise low-rank context/history product correction
Original auxiliary scorer/item/action/tower-context gradient gates and adapter-context transfer
Max-absolute detached-FP32 pivot chart from g1-r0067-coarse_axis (helper convention verified in supplied g1-r0069 sources)
study.proposed_difference: A 2x2 factorial selects raw signed coarse moment versus its max-coordinate canonical axis independently for the residual-bank input and the history-projection input. Every cell constructs both signals every forward; only selection switches differ. Compute chart after original per-task gradient gating. Both-signed is the contemporaneous unchanged bridge; both-axis bridges the previous coarse-axis replacement. No scalar feature, learned parameter, loss hook, event rearrangement or other moment change. Treat this as attribution of a failed representation replacement, with novelty unverified.
predictions: For A_ah with a=adapter sign and h=interaction sign, require gap G=A_11-A_00 >=0.0005 before using recovery fractions. Predicted (A_01-A_00)/G >=0.75 and (A_10-A_00)/G <=0.25.

Predeclare conditional effects d_h|a=0=A_01-A_00, d_h|a=1=A_11-A_10, d_a|h=0=A_10-A_00, d_a|h=1=A_11-A_01 and interaction I=A_11-A_10-A_01+A_00. Large positive I supports joint dependence rather than either route alone.

Both-signed should match incumbent at copied state in outputs, gradients, Dice buffers and optimizer step within measured numerical tolerance; both-axis should implement the same moment replacement as g1-r0067-coarse_axis without new parameters. Expected all cells: 32192421 total, 31793216 embedding, 399205 dense parameters.

History>64 may have a larger orientation effect, based on earlier exploratory slices. Report existing four bins with counts; this is exploratory, with no new confirmatory slice claim. No speed gain is predicted from sign routing; measure actual overhead.
falsifiers: Endpoint gap G<0.0005 makes the proposed fractional recovery test inconclusive; do not normalize a tiny or reversed gap.

Interaction-only recovery <75% or adapter-only recovery >25% contradicts the specific dominant-product-path hypothesis. Similar partial gains indicate shared use; a large positive factorial interaction indicates coordinated dependence.
If either one-route cell equals or exceeds both-signed, indispensable signed availability in both consumers is falsified for this training setting; evaluate cost before retaining a simplification.

Native endpoint parity, input isolation, masking, gradient ownership or budget gates fail: stop, record charged failure, and correct implementation before interpreting AUC. A source/algebra check alone is not native validation.
Failure across one frozen seed is preliminary and does not refute all decoding architectures or prove useful whole-history order dependence.
alternative_explanations: Single frozen seed and adaptive trajectory selection; no independent seed replication yet
Removing a learned-coordinate sign changes embedding gradients and optimization, and leaves other supplied-order channels intact
The pivot chart is piecewise discontinuous and parameter-dependent; a null does not establish information-theoretic order irrelevance
Adapter and product branches share upstream embeddings and final task towers; factorial attribution is conditional on joint retraining
Single-pass learning may fail to learn the pivot chart; direct signed routing avoids that decoding problem without resolving causal event-order utility
Native BF16 accumulation and scorer normalization differences may explain small effects; common-state endpoint checks are mandatory
